title: Decision Lattice for Phased Experiments and Quantified Rollback Thresholds
creator: Ayesha Malik
description: Goal: Create a prescriptive decision lattice (decision tree + thresholds) for running phased experiments (A/B tests, lightweight canaries, staged rollouts) that makes go/no-go decisions deterministic and observable. This ticket captures the product-side spec, acceptance criteria, and milestone cadence needed to deliver a ship-ready orchestration guide and dashboard hooks for Q1 experiments.
background: We run many lightweight canaries and A/B experiments to validate performance, cost, and quality changes (eg. kernel selection, KV cache heuristics, quantization profiles). Currently decisions rely on ad-hoc thresholds and human judgment; teams have asked for a standardized lattice with numeric thresholds (latency, error, quality regressions, token-cost delta) and explicit escalation paths so rollouts are faster and less error-prone.
hypothesis: If we provide a simple, audited decision lattice with clear numeric thresholds and automated signal checks, teams will reduce mean time-to-rollback for regressions and increase safe experiment velocity by 30% within one quarter.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A published Decision Lattice doc (Confluence) that defines at least three phased experiment types (smoke/canary, progressive A/B, ramp-to-100) and the exact signal thresholds used for automated gating.
A2: Console dashboard mock with widget designs for: canary health overview, metric deltas, and rollback button wired to ops playbook links.
A3: A sample canary rollout executed end-to-end (internal test) using the lattice that demonstrates automatic stop at defined thresholds and generates an audit log entry.
A4: A runbook for on-call with clear escalation ladder and post-mortem template attached.
A5: Stakeholder signoff from Eng Reliability, Security, and 2 PMs running experiments.
milestones: M1 (Discovery, 1 week): Gather 12 previous experiment post-mortems, collect common failure modes and observed metric deltas.
M2 (Spec & thresholds, 2 weeks): Define numeric thresholds for core signals (p50/p95/p99 latency delta, error rate increase, token-cost delta, quality regression on eval set).
M3 (Console mocks + API hooks, 2 weeks): Design dashboard widgets and minimal API endpoints for gating checks and forced rollback.
M4 (Pilot canary, 1 week): Run internal pilot against stage models, validate alerts and automatic gating logic.
M5 (Rollout + docs, 1 week): Publish lattice, runbook, and ship console widgets as beta to internal teams.
signals_and_thresholds: Latency: P99 increase > 20% over baseline OR absolute P99 > 800ms -> fail for low-latency routes.
Errors: 5xx spike > 2x baseline (3-minute rolling window) OR error rate > 0.5% absolute -> immediate stop.
Quality: Eval-set BLEU/ROUGE or custom pass-rate drop > 3 percentage points -> stop and notify quality owners.
Cost: Token-cost per 1k tokens increases by > 25% without commensurate quality gain -> pause rollout and require approval.
SLOs: Any SLO breach during canary (latency or availability) triggers automatic rollback and incident creation.
runbook_high_level: If canary fails automated gating, the system must: 1) mark rollout as paused, 2) notify experiment owner and reliability on-call, 3) capture sample traces and a diff of metric windows, 4) surface rollback button in console.
On manual override: PM must fill short justification template and tag reliability lead; override creates audit log with user and timestamp.
Post-rollback: owner must open a post-mortem within 48 hours linking the experiment ID and include remediation plan.
ui_requirements: Canary health card with current phase, pass/fail status, overall score and top contributing metrics.
Metric delta sparklines with hoverable windows and links to traces and PR that introduced the change.
Rollback CTA (disabled until fail condition met) that triggers assembled runbook checklist on click.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-sensitive thresholds cause frequent false rollbacks. Mitigation: require two consecutive failing windows or a confidence check (statistical significance) before automatic rollback for low-impact experiments.
Risk: Complex lattice is ignored by teams. Mitigation: Provide templates and one-click experiment scaffold in Console to adopt lattice by default.
Risk: Signal noise from region variance. Mitigation: Run canaries by region and require global failure for cross-region automatic rollback.
